subject: Request: Performance penalty structure and termination carve-outs
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medazio.health>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
Cc: procure@medazio.health
Date: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask: penalties & termination carve-outs

Rishi — thanks again for the demo last week. Medazio is finalizing an internal compliance checklist and our legal/finance teams are pushing for stronger commercial remedies for production-impacting incidents. Two asks they want to include in the contract:

- A fee-at-risk pool (3 months of committed spend) held in escrow to be released on repeated SLA misses (defined as monthly uptime < 99.5 on rolling 3-month window).
- A termination right for cause if we hit 3 severity-1 incidents in a 12-month period, with liquidated damages equal to 6 months of committed fees if we exercise termination.

We understand Redwood provides credits today, but these teams require tangible fee recapture and termination options for highly regulated customers. Attaching our redlines for context (Medazio_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf). Can you share whether Redwood can accommodate any of these? If not, what mitigation we can offer that would be acceptable to procurement and finance?

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director, Cloud Procurement
Medazio Health

Attachment: Medazio_SLA_Redlines_v3.pdf
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medazio.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA ask: penalties & termination carve-outs

Hi Alicia — thanks for sharing the redlines and the ask. I ran this past legal and commercial; a few quick points up front:

- Redwood's standard commercial remedy is service credits tied to severity and duration of outages. We do not typically accept liquidated damages or cash refunds tied to uptime, because it creates open-ended financial exposure and materially changes our pricing structure.
- Termination for repeated incidents is something we can discuss, but we try to narrow triggers (e.g., documented failure to cure after escalation and remediation steps) rather than an automatic termination after N incidents.

That said, I want to be constructive. Proposed middle ground we can put in writing: 
1) Escrow-style fee-at-risk: we can agree to a modest retained fee (capped at 1 month of committed spend) held against the first provable compliance breach after an agreed cure process. Release mechanics: upon resolution and agreed post-mortem, funds are released unless a repeat breach occurs within 6 months.
2) Enhanced termination clause: allow for termination for cause only after (a) severity-1 incident confirmed by both parties, (b) failure to meet a defined remediation plan within 30 days, and (c) two such uncured incidents within a 12-month rolling window. If termination is exercised, the remedy would be a limited break fee equal to 2 months of committed spend (not full liquidated damages).

If that framing is acceptable, I'll loop in legal and customer success to draft language and propose concrete SLO definitions and measurement windows. Appreciate you surfacing this — we want to be a reliable partner, and we also need to manage commercial risk.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SLA ask: penalties & termination carve-outs

Rishi / Karthik — quick internal note before I respond to Alicia. A couple negotiation levers to consider:

- We can accept an escrow-like construct only for enterprise reserved deals (they're committing to a 12mo rec). If Medazio is doing Dedicated, this is more palatable.
- Cap is critical. Karthik, legal will push back on liquidated damages language; recommend we avoid that term and instead call it a "termination break fee" with a hard dollar cap tied to committed spend.
- Measurement: insist on telemetry and thresholds we own (Redwood metrics) or mutually agreed third-party monitoring to avoid disputes.
- Cure process and runbook: make sure it includes automatic failover options and interim mitigation (e.g., fallbacks to a lower-capacity variant) so we can avoid immediate terminations.

I'll propose the compromise Rishi suggested and add the Dedicated-only condition. Thoughts?

-M
Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.example
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@medazio.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example, procure@medazio.health
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA ask: penalties & termination carve-outs

Alicia — following internal review and Marissa's notes, here's a concrete proposal we can put into the SOW for Medazio if you are on a 12-month Dedicated commitment:

1) Fee-at-risk: Redwood will escrow an amount equal to 1 month of committed fees. Triggers: a documented SLA breach (monthly uptime < 99.5) where Redwood's internal telemetry confirms the breach after standard investigation. Cure: 30 days to remediate. If the same breach repeats within 6 months after remediation, escrowed funds transfer to Medazio.

2) Termination carve-out: Medazio may terminate for cause only after (i) a confirmed severity-1 incident, (ii) failure to meet an agreed remediation plan within 30 days, and (iii) two uncured severity-1 incidents in a rolling 12-month window. If termination is exercised under this clause, Redwood will pay a termination break fee capped at 2 months of committed fees. No liquidated damages beyond that.

3) Measurement & dispute resolution: all SLO breaches will be determined from Redwood's monitoring by default; either party can request a joint post-mortem and third-party metric review if there's a dispute.

4) Exceptions: prolonged force majeure events and customer-induced outages (misconfigurations, denial-of-service triggered by customer configuration) are excluded.

If that aligns with your legal/finance team's needs, we can have our counsel redline the exact clause language and share a DocuSign for the SOW addendum. Happy to hop on a short call to walk through the mechanics.

Best,
Rishi
Head of GTM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Performance_Metrics_Summary_2026Q2.xlsx
